t: A Turkic steppe state between the Volga and the Caucasus, ruled jointly by a sacral khagan and a military bek.
It held back Arab expansion north of the Caucasus and taxed the Volga trade linking the Islamic world to Northern Europe.
Its ruling elite famously converted to Judaism; Sviatoslav of Kiev's campaign of the 960s brought the khaganate down.
dyk: The Byzantine emperor Constantine V married the Khazar princess Tzitzak, and their son reigned as Leo IV, known as 'the Khazar'.
ev: The khaganate emerges on the Pontic-Caspian steppe as the Western Turkic Khaganate fragments
The Khazars destroy an Arab army at Marj Ardabil
Marwan ibn Muhammad's great campaign forces a temporary Khazar submission
The fortress of Sarkel is built on the Don with Byzantine engineers
Sviatoslav I of Kiev captures Sarkel and sacks Atil, dismantling the khaganate
